The purpose of this study is to present modern paleomagnetic data from five Oligocene-aged volcanic
provincesincentralQueensland,innortheasternAustralia,andtoprovideasynthesiswithexistingdatafor

Accepted7JUN2019 Australiafromthisepoch.AlthoughtheearliestpaleomagneticresultsfromAustralianolongermeetmod-
Acceptedarticleonline13JUN2019 erncriteriaforpaleomagneticdata(sampleswerenotdemagnetized;Green&Irving,1958;Irving&Green,
Publishedonline24JUL2019 1958;Irvingetal.,1961),manystudiesfromtheCenozoicerathatwereconductedsincehavefallenout
ofuseduetooutdatedblanketdemagnetizationtechniques,leavinggapsinthecontinentalpaleomagnetic
record.WhilesomevalidationoftheseresultshasbeenaccomplishedforpartsoftheCenozoicera(specifi-
callyarevisionofNewerVolcanicProvinceresults,Aziz-Ur-Rahman,1971;Opdyke&Musgrave,2004;and
validationofearlierBarringtonVolcano,Hilletal.,2002;Wellmanetal.,1969;NandewarVolcanoandthe
PortCampbellandGlenampleFormationsresults,Hansma&Tohver,2018;Idnurm,1985;Wellmanetal.,
1969),Oligoceneresultsremaintobeexamined.AdramaticincreaseinAustralia'snorthwarddriftatthe
beginningoftheOligocene(∼ 34Ma)isindicatedbyseafloormagneticanomalypatternsintheSouthern
Ocean,withaccelerationoccurringafteranomalyC13(Tikku&Cande,1999).Globalplatemodelspredicta
doublingofAustralia'sapparentpolarwander(APW)rateafterC13,from∼0.3◦/Mabetween60and34Ma
to∼0.6–0.7◦/Mabetween34and0Ma(Matthewsetal.,2016;Setonetal.,2012).However,paleomagnetic
documentationofthistransitiontorapiddriftratesisnotclearfromexistingapparentpolarwanderpaths
(APWPs;Idnurm,1985,1994;McElhinnyetal.,1974;Musgrave,1989).
WhilepublishedOligocenepaleomagneticresultsforAustraliaexist,thesevenigneousresultsareblan-
ket demagnetized, whereas stepwise demagnetization is limited to a pair of results from sedimentary
rocks, preventing evaluation of seafloor spreading model predictions (Idnurm, 1985, 1994; McElhinny
etal.,1974;Mumme,1963;Robertson,1966;Wellman,1975;Wellmanetal.,1969).Excessivefilteringof
blanket-demagnetizedsampleswasidentifiedbyMusgrave(1989)asthecauseofunrealisticzigzagsinthe
APWPofMcElhinnyetal.(1974).Priortothisrealization,however,thesedeviationsfalselyimpliedepisodic
volcanismand,byextension,inadequatesamplingofpaleosecularvariation(PSV).Assuch,focusshifted
togeneratingsedimentarypaleomagneticresults,culminatinginanAPWPthatrejectedalmostallpaleo-

2.GeologicalBackgroundandSampling
RemnantsofOligocenehotspotvolcanismareexposedalonga∼450-km-longnorth-southlinearchainin
centralQueenslandfromCapeHillsboroughtoBucklandVolcano(Figure1).Therocksweregeneratedby
theCosgrovehotspot,that,alongwithleucititelavaspreservedinNewSouthWalesandVictoria,formsthe
longestcontinentalhotspottrackonEarth(Daviesetal.,2015;Sutherland,1981).TheCosgrovetrackis
thewesternmostoffivesouthwardyoungingCenozoichotspottracksontheeasternAustralianPlate,with
ComboyneandCanobolashotspotshavingproducedtwootheronshorehotspottracksandtheTasmantid
andLordHowehotspotshavingproducedtwooffshoretracks.Finite-frequencytomographyindicatesthat
theCosgrovehotspotitselflies∼ 300kmbeneathnortheasternTasmaniaandtheBassStrait(Montelli
etal.,2006).
ThecentralQueenslandsegmentoftheCosgrovetrackisfurtherdividedintofiveprogressivelyyounger
volcanicprovincesthatrepresentvolcanicactivityfrom34MaatHillsboroughVolcano,followedbyNebo
(33–32 Ma), Peak Range (31–28 Ma), Springsure (28.5–27.5 Ma), and Buckland Volcanoes (28–27 Ma;
Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013).Thevolcanosineachprovinceareshieldsofchemicallybimodalcomposition,
consistingofvariablyerodedbasalticlavas,accompaniedbylatestagesilicicvolcanism.
Basalts have tholeiitic composition and commonly contain olivine and plagioclase phenocrysts, set in a
groundmass also containing pyroxene, and accessory titanomagnetite, ilmenite, and apatite. Silicic rock

basalt-type,metasomatizedmantlesource(EM-1type)withlittlecrustalassimilation(Daviesetal.,2015;
Ewart,1982).
TheextrusivevolumeofeachcentralQueenslandvolcanicprovincehasbeenestimatedat∼500km3,with
perhapstwiceasmuchvolumeofintrusivematerial(Wellman&McDougall,1974).Thinnerlithosphere
andmeltingatshallowercrustaldepths(<110km)ledtosignificantlygreatervolumesofmeltproduction

restrictedmelting,producingleucititeslavas(Daviesetal.,2015).
2.1.Sampling
Multipleorientedsamples(7–10cores)werecollectedfromoutcropusingagasoline-poweredPomeroydrill
at94individualsites,thatis,coolingunits(81ofwhichproducedconsistentwithin-sitemagnetizations).
Basalticsiteswerecollectedfromroadcutandstreambedexposures,aswellasinciseddrainagebeneath
siliciccappedmesas.Silicicrockswerealsotakenfromroadcuts,aswellasatthebaseoflarge,natural
exposures.SitelocationwasrecordedwithhandheldGPS,andsampleorientationwastakenbymagnetic
andsolarcompass.MagneticorientationswerecorrectedusingWMM2015-2025(Chulliatetal.,2015)and,
inmostcases,corroboratedsolarazimuths,differingby<5◦.Inthefewcaseswherelocalmagneticazimuths
deviatedbygreateramounts,solarazimuthsweregivenpreference.Threepairsofsites,PR18andPR19,
PR20andPR21,andHV16andHV17,weretakenfromthesameflow/felsicintrusion,andsampleswere
combined.Ofthefivevolcanicprovincessampled,Springsureistheonlyonewherepreviouspaleomagnetic
workhastakenplace,comprisingsevensitesfromMountBoorambool(McElhinnyetal.,1974).
2.2.Buckland
Buckland Volcano is an ∼ 80-km-wide shield volcano erupted onto Jurassic sandstones. Clear radial
drainageispreserved(Young&Wray,2000),and∼ 300mofhorizontalbasalticlavathicknessremains,
formingtablelandtopography(Skae,1998).Flowsarecomposedofbasalts,trachybasalts,andhighlyalka-
linebasaniticlavas,withthreeminorfelsicintrusionsfoundnearthecenterofthevolcano(Skae,1998).
Anothergroupofalkalimaficplugsandflowslie∼ 60kmSWofthemainvolcaniccenter(Mollanetal.,
1969;Skae,1998).An40Ar∕39Artotalfusionageof27.3±0.4Mafromsanidineofperalkalinetrachyteplug
(Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013)iscompatiblewithfissiontrackageof27.6±1.1Ma(Hollis&Sutherland,1985).
Tenpaleomagneticsitesofbasalticflows(BV1–BV10)weresampled(Figure1).
2.3.Springsure
SpringsurevolcanositsatopLowerPermiansandstonesandhasacentralzoneofsilicicplugsandflows,
theMinervaHillsVolcanics,surroundedbymesasandplainsofmaficlava(Cohen,Withnall,etal.,2013).
Lavaflowshaveamaximumthicknessof∼330mnearthevolcanocenter,withlavasbeingbroadlydivided
intolowermaficflows,interbeddedmaficandsilicicflowsthatincludetheMinervaHillsplugs,andupper
maficflows(Mollanetal.,1969;Sutherlandetal.,1989).Theflowsincludeolivinebasaltandlessbasic,
intermediate,lavas.ThepyroclasticsnearSpringsureconsistofmassivereddishpurplescoriaceoustuffsof
trachyticcompositionandwell-beddedoff-whitefinerhyoliticagglomerateandtuff(Mollanetal.,1969;
Sutherlandetal.,1989).TheMinervaHillsVolcanicsconsistofasuiteofalkalinerocksrangingfromtrachyte
toalkalinerhyolite.Theyarepreservedmainlyasdykes,plugs,anddomes,butadissectedseriesofflowsare
alsopresent.An40Ar∕39Artotalfusionanalysisofsanidinefromasilicicintrusiongaveanage28.1±0.3Ma
(Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013).Fifteenpaleomagneticsitesofmaficandsilicicunitsweresampledfromthis
provincethat,togetherwithsevenpreviouslypublishedsitesfromMountBoorambool(McElhinnyetal.,
1974),comprisethe22sitessampled.
2.4.PeakRange
ThePeakRangevolcanicfieldstretchesover100kminaN-Sdirectionwitholder,silicicplugsinthenorth
(30.7±0.4and30.3±0.4Ma),mesasofmaficlavasinthecenter(30.4±0.5Ma),andyoungersilicicplugs
inthesouth(29.0±0.4and28.6±0.4Ma;Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013;Cohen,Withnall,etal.,2013).The
northernplugsareperaluminousrhyolites,whilethesouthernplugsareperalkalinerhyolitesandtrachytes
(Cohen,Withnall,etal.,2013).Surroundingtheplugsaremaficlavas,commonlycoveredbysoilbutexposed
inriverbedsandroadcuttings.IncentralPeakRange,theresidualmesasofLord'sTableMountainattestto

2.5.Nebo
Nebo volcano hosts numerous, partly eroded mafic flows, although extensive weathering and lateritiza-
tionoftheseunitshasoccurredsinceOligocenetimespreventingpaleomagneticsamplingoftherocksin
theregion.Relativelymoreresistantsilicicshallowintrusivesarescatteredthroughouttheareaandwere
moreamenabletosampling,albeitbeingmoreremotecomparedwithotherprovincesdescribedhere,pre-
venting more extensive sampling. Seven paleomagnetic sites of rhyolitic tuff, flow banded rhyolite, and
trachyteplugsweresampled,thesebeingpreservedascliffsandescarpments.Sanidinefromatrachytedyke
intrudingsilicicpyroclasticsyieldedan40Ar∕39Arageof32.6±0.4Ma(Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013).
2.6.Hillsborough
HillsboroughistheoldestvolcanoalongtheCosgrovehotspottrack.An40Ar∕39Arageof33.6±0.5Ma
fromfeldsparofatMountJukesconstrainstheageofthevolcano(Cohen,Knesel,etal.,2013).Thelargest
remnantofthisvolcanoisexposedatCapeHillsborough,wherea∼350-m-thickseriesofflows,pyroclas-
tics,andrhyoliticplugsarepreserved(McDougall&Slessar,1972).Theremainderofthevolcanoismore
heavilyeroded,withitsdeeperplumbingsystem,theMountJukesIntrusiveComplex,nowexposedatthe
surfaceandwithisolatedremnantsofcolumnarjointedtrachytealsopresentintheprovince.Twenty-four
paleomagneticsitesweresampledfromthisprovince.
3.RockMagneticAnalysisandAnisotropyofMagneticSusceptibility
3.1.Susceptibility-TemperatureCurves
Inordertodeterminemagneticmineralogyanddemagnetizationcharacteristicsateachsite,smallvolumes
ofcrushedrockwereprepared,weighed,andthenloadedintoquartzglassholdersandmagneticsuscep-
tibilitychangeswithtemperature(K -Tcurves)measuredusinganAgicoMFK-1kappabridgewithCS-4
m
furnace.Sampleswereheatedfromroomtemperatureto700◦Candcooledbacktoroomtemperatureinan
inertatmosphere.Samplesgenerallyshowirreversiblebehaviortheprecisenatureofwhichvariesbetween
sitesofdifferentlithologiesandmagneticmineralogies,withexamplesofbothlowerandhigherfinalsus-
ceptibilitythaninitialvalues,aswellascomplexcurvesrelatedtomineralbreakdownandgrowthofnew
magnetites(FigureS1).Inspiteofthis,K-Tcurvesaredominatedbysteeplydecayingheatingcurveswith
Curietemperaturesof∼ 580◦C,diagnosticoftitanium-poormagnetite.Ti-richmagnetitesoccurredbut
weremorerarelyencountered(FigureS1,PR2.2).Curiepoints> 600◦Cwerenotobserved,andhematite
is an extremely uncommon magnetic phase. In spite of this, thermal demagnetization of pilot samples
fromafewsitesdidrevealsmallamountsofstableremanenceabove580◦Cthatweredemagnetizedby
675◦C,suggestingafewcasesofhematite(inferredbyareddishcolorationofthesesamples)ormaghemite
occurringincoexistencewithmagnetite.Areductioninsusceptibilityduringheatingisobservedinsome
samples,suggestingthatsomealterationiscausedbyheating.K -T curvesrangefromnearlyreversible
m
(FigureS1,BV8.4),toexampleswithdramaticdifferences,suggestingthermalinversionofmorestrongly
magnetizedmaterialsduringheating(FigureS1,SV9.4andPR35.7).Coolingcurveswithhigherfinalsus-
ceptibilitiesthaninitialvaluesindicatednewlyformedmagnetite,probablyproducedbyoxy-exolutionof
titanomagnetiteorilmenite(FigureS1,HV25.5andHV8.7).Unlesspilotthermaldemagnetizationrevealed
aremanenceabovethemagnetiteCuriepoint,oralternatingfield(AF)demagnetizationprovedineffec-
tive,AFdemagnetizationwaschosentominimizethedetrimentaleffectsthatneoformationofmagnetite
particlesmighthaveonisolatingcharacteristicremanencecomponents.
3.2.AnisotropyofMagneticSusceptibility
Anisotropyofmagneticsusceptibility(AMS)ellipsoidsweremeasuredonmultiplesamplesfromeachsite,
to examine the preservation of flow fabrics and primary flow dips and to evaluate the possibility of any
tilting that may have gone unrecognized during fieldwork. Bulk susceptibility (K ) is positively skewed m
from3.65×10−5to6.29×10−2SI,withsignificantlyhighervaluesinmaficrocks(median=1.38×10−2SI)
thaninfelsicrocks(median=0.33×10−2SI,FigureS2).Degreesofanisotropy(P)aregenerallylow,and
j
theirdistributionispositivelyskewedfromisotropicvalues(P ≤ 1.01)to1.14atthemostextreme,witha
j
medianof1.02,consistentwiththeundeformednatureofvolcanicmaterialsampled.Thereisnosignificant
differenceindegreeofanisotropybetweenmaficandfelsicrocks.TheshapeofAMSellipsoidsarevariable
betweenspecimensandrangefromveryprolate(T=−0.984;K −K )toveryoblate(T=0.986;K −K )with

5.Australia'sAPWPDuringtheCenozoic
Wewishedtoseeifcontinentalpaleomagneticdatawerecompatiblewithevidencefromseafloorspreading
fortheAustralianPlate.OfparticularinteresttouswastheaccelerationoftheAustralianplatenorthward,

1989).
TogenerateaCenozoicAPWPforAustralia,werecalculatedseveralmorecombinedpolesforAustraliadur-
ingtheCenozoic,usingthesamesitemeanVGPlevelapproachdescribedabove(Table4).APlio-Pleistocene

2004).Themid-MiocenecombinedpolepresentedinHansmaandTohver(2018)wascalculatedwiththe

1963;Embletonetal.,1985;Manwaring,1963;McElhinnyetal.,1974;Robertson,1979).Ouroldestpale-
omagneticpoleisofLatePaleocene-EarlyEoceneage(50–60Ma)andcombinesresultsfromBarrington
VolcanobyHilletal.(2002),whoseresultscorroboratebutsupercedeearlierblanketdemagnetizationby

butmorecommonlyappliedmeanage,tobethemagnetizationageofthepole.

continental Paleocene paleomagnetic data from Australia. While Whittaker et al. (2007) point out that
therotations(Tikku&Cande,1999)usedintheSetonetal.(2012)modelproduceunacceptableoverlaps
betweentheSouthTasmanRiseandEastAntarctica,unrealisticepisodesofextensionandcompression
of the Kerguelen Plateau present in both models led to further revision (Whittaker et al., 2013). The
Whittaker et al. (2013) model resolves both aforementioned fit problems and is also compatible with
Australiancontinentalpaleomagneticdata.
DetectingchangesinratesofplatemotionusingpaleomagneticdataisultimatelydictatedbyVGPscatter
andbygeologicalpreservation.ItiswellknownthatVGPscattercausedbyPSVisgreaterthancontinen-
talmotionovershorttimescales,butoverthelong-termtectonicdriftalsomatters.Asitisassumedthat
VGPs are independent of one another and as there are simply a limited number of magmatic units and
sedimentary beds on a continent for any given period of time, geological preservation ultimately limits
paleomagnetic precision, setting a practical limit on what might feasibly be observable using paleomag-
netictechniques.SpatialandtemporalbiasesintroducedintoAPWPsalsocancontributetoobscuringthose
changesthatmaybeobservableintheVGPdatathatunderliethem.Positionalbiasintroducedbyaverag-
ingpolesratherthantheirunderlyingVGPdistributionscanbiasposition,whilecommonAPWPaveraging
methodscanalsoobscuretectonicchangespresentintheunderlyingdata.Greatersplinesmoothingfac-
torsincreaseagedecouplingbetweentheAPWPandtheunderlyingVGPdistribution(VanderVoo,1993),
whileinmoving-windowapproaches,byassumingapoleagetobethecenterofaninterval,ratherthanthe
morerobustmedianVGPagewithinthatinterval,asimilardecouplingcanalsobeintroduced.
6.Conclusions
WehavepresentedpaleomagneticresultsfromfiveOligocenevolcanicprovincesoftheCosgrovehotspot
track in central Queensland and compared these with the body of already published Oligocene paleo-
magneticdata.Thegoodagreementbetweenresultsobtainedwithmoderntechniquesandolderresults,
bothindirectionandVGPscatter,validatemanyexistingresults,withonlyresultsfromCentralProvince
(McElhinnyetal.,1974)andOlderVolcanics(Mumme,1963)beingsuspectinthisregard.Weshowthat
magneticvectorsfrom97sitesalongtheCosgrovehotspotareconsistentwithexpecteddistributionsbased
ontheTK03geomagneticfieldmodel(Tauxe&Kent,2004).WepresentedacombinedOligocenepolebased
onsite-meanVGPleveldataandcombineditwithpoledatafromtherestoftheCenozoicera,confirm-
ingthatcontinentalpaleomagneticdatafromAustraliareflectachangeinrateofmotion,compatiblewith
acceleratedseafloorspreadingintheSouthernOceanafteranomalyC13(∼34Ma).
